title.narrative: Provision of a multisector life-saving response to the affected populations in the WagHimra Zone, Amhara Region,Dehana Woredas

description.narrative: ltpgtAction Against Hunger developed a multi-sector humanitarian response that includes nutrition, health, agriculture, WASH, and protection as mainstream in order to address the emergency needs of IDPs and host communities affected by conflict and drought in Dehana Woredas of Wag Himra Zone, Amhara region. This intervention will address a total of 87,917 beneficiaries, out of which 62% are females and 43% are children. The nutrition initiative will support the selected target beneficiaries by admitting and treating children under five in SC, treating SAM children under five without medical complications in OTP. In addition Supporting woreda offices on the procurement of non-food items (stationary, hygiene, and sanitation materials) and essential drugs to ensure continuity of services, conducting modular training on SAM treatment for frontline healthcare providers, Selecting and supporting IYCF-E including the provision of IYCF counseling services, Sensitizing MtMSGs and FtFSG on IYCF health education and promotion activities, integrating nutrition and psychosocial mother-to-mother support groups (MtMSGs), and establishing one baby-friendly space through nutrition intervention. A total of 37,041 persons from Dehana Wereda of whom 72% are female and 50% are children will benefit from the nutrition intervention. In the same vein, the initiative will also intervene through health by organizing annual health days to raise awareness on selected health topics within the community, mobilizing community members and implementing health education sessions within health facilities to educate patients and caregivers on RMNCAH issues, providing capacity-building training, providing essential hygiene and infection prevention and control (IPC) materials, Procure gap-filling life-saving essential medications for static health facilities rehabilitation, including minor maintenance, ceiling work, metal wood work, and painting ensure the effectiveness and quality of routine as well as campaign vaccinations and other RMNCH services facilitate coordination, learning, and continuous improvement hold quarterly review meetings strengthen disease surveillance systems and provide logistical support for prepositioning or responding to different public health emergencies. As a result of the health intervention, a total of 56,604 beneficiaries will be reached, of whom 51% are female and 53% are children. The project will also promote green leafy and nutrient-rich vegetable production and consumption, support egg production and consumption through procuring and distributing locally adapted layer chicken selected in consultation with the Bureau of Agriculture and community representatives and promote nutrition-sensitive agriculture practices through field-based practical training through agricultural intervention with the support of 2,500 beneficiaries (51% are females) in Dehana woreda. Emergency WASH response addresses the immediate lifesaving needs of the drought-affected community through the rehabilitation and expansion of nonfunctional water schemes, the establishment and training of WASH Committee members, the rehabilitation of health care facilities and sanitation facilities (sex segregated latrines, hand washing stations) in affected health institutions, and the and the provision of lifesaving WASH NFI and water treatment products at the household level. Hygiene and sanitation promotion will be addressed to a total of 10,500 beneficiaries (51 % are female) through WASH intervention.lt/pgt
